newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut's Solidere down in profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Beirut's Solidere down in profit taking.

text.p: Shares in Solidere dropped again in profit taking on Friday, winding down from a two-week surge to the highest levels in two years on the Beirut Stock Exchange.
Banks remained strong. Banque Audi hit a high of $28.6250, up from $28.5. Banque Libanais pour le Commerce stayed at a high of $21.5. Bank of Beirut also kept a record level of $4.6875.
Solidere A shares dropped to $12.8750 from $13.125 on Wednesday when BSE shares were last traded and B shares fell to the same level from $13.50.
"There was a huge supply of shares because of profit-taking. It's an adjustment for Solidere," said one broker.
The LIBX bank index climbed 0.15 percent to 185.34. The BLOM general index dropped 2.40 percent to 1101.67 and the LISPI general index fell 0.56 percent to 95.19.
BSE turnover took a steep fall to 291,908 shares for a value of $3,519,732 against 832,541 shares for a value of $11,455,359.
"Demand for the share is too small. Those planning to buy are waiting to come in at lower prices," another broker said.
Financial markets were closed on Thursday to mark the Prophet Mohammad's birthday.
Ciment Libanais moved up to $1.2813 from $1.2800 when it was last traded on July 14.
There was no trade in the other three listed industrial firms -- Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic. -- Beirut editorial (9611) 745307 745308 602057
